package_info.why_malicious: These Word document templates are weaponized to exploit CVE-2017-0199, enabling remote code execution via embedded and downloaded malicious Visual Basic and PowerShell scripts. The infection chain leads to the download and execution of Cobalt Strike, RedLine Infostealer, and Amadey Botnet payloads, all of which are well-known malware families.

execution_context.trigger: document open (user opens malicious Word file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Embedded Visual Basic script exploiting CVE-2017-0199 to download and execute further scripts.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon document open, the embedded VB script exploits CVE-2017-0199 to download and execute a remote DOTM template, which in turn executes additional obfuscated VB and PowerShell scripts, leading to payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not execute code that downloads and runs additional scripts or executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents do not contain code that exploits vulnerabilities to execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document templates may use macros for document formatting, but not for code execution or remote downloads.
key_indicators: Automatic download and execution of remote scripts

execution_context.trigger: macro execution (triggered by document open or user action)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated Visual Basic script that downloads and executes a Windows executable.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After macro execution, the VB script downloads a Windows executable from a remote server and executes it, which then runs malicious PowerShell commands to implant malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros should not download and execute arbitrary executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate macros are used for document automation, not for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise environments use macros for automation, but not for downloading executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious PowerShell commands executed by the Windows executable to download and implant Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the executable runs PowerShell commands that download additional payloads (Cobalt Strike, RedLine, Amadey) from remote servers and execute them, establishing persistence and C2 communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executables launched by Office macros should not execute PowerShell to download and run further malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not chain execution from Office macros to PowerShell-based malware downloaders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: PowerShell is used for legitimate automation, but not in this chained, obfuscated, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Network download of known malware payloads

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Word document, triggering embedded VB script exploiting CVE-2017-0199.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote DOTM template with further malicious scripts.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded DOTM template executes obfuscated VB script to download and run a Windows executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of Windows executable that runs malicious PowerShell.

attack_chain.action: Windows executable runs PowerShell commands to download and implant Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of C2, data exfiltration, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Macros downloading and executing remote scripts or binaries
PowerShell execution from unknown or recently downloaded executables
Chained execution: Office macro -> executable -> PowerShell -> malware
file_indicators: Obfuscated macro code in DOTM templates
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199 and containing obfuscated macros that download and execute remote scripts or binaries. Detect PowerShell execution originating from Office processes or unknown executables, especially those that download known malware payloads. Correlate network activity to known malicious Bitbucket URLs and C2 IPs. Use file hashes and ClamAV signatures provided to identify known payloads.
